rule: Public GitHub repositories that keep decision records or deprecation notices, in three groups. In each group the candidates are every repository of that kind we could name with the group's minimum of stars, most stars first, and the first `take` that pass the group's check are taken: the check looks only at whether the records named are in the tree, never at what the readers find in them.

groups.title: Decision archives
groups.rule: A repository that holds the proposals of a language, framework or protocol (PEPs, RFCs, KEPs, EIPs, BIPs, NIPs, MSCs, design documents, or a tracking list of them), 1,000 stars or more. Check: a file of the records named is in the tree.

groups.title: Decision records in a project's own tree
groups.rule: A well-known project, 1,000 stars or more, that keeps its own decision records (ADRs, RFCs, RFDs, design proposals or specs) in a folder of its main repository. Check: a record in that folder is in the tree.

groups.title: Deprecation notices in a changelog
groups.rule: A well-known project, 10,000 stars or more, that keeps deprecation notices in a changelog: a file named CHANGELOG, CHANGES, HISTORY or RELEASES (any extension, any folder) whose text says "deprecat" at least once. Check: such a file is in the tree.
